stem:
Leena leaves muddy water undisturbed in a tall glass. After the mud settles, she carefully pours off the clearer water.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: Sedimentation lets heavier mud settle, and decantation pours off the liquid above it.
The settling of mud at the bottom is itself called decantation.
The same settling-and-pour method will separate dissolved salt from salt water.
After pouring, no tiny mud particle can remain in the liquid that was poured off.

teacher.key_rationale: Sedimentation is settling of heavier matter; decantation is pouring off the liquid above. Settling is not decantation. Dissolved salt does not settle for this method. Some fine particles may remain after pouring.
